formalization.definition: E_mod is residue reduction; E_strict accepts exactly the representable unsigned 42-bit interval.
formalization.evidence_boundary: Encoding policy definition; does not establish novelty or cryptographic security.

steps: Modulo 2^42 has a unique residue in [0,2^42).
Inside that range the residue equals x.
The strict encoder is defined to reject all other integers.

formalization.theorem: E_mod always returns a representable residue; E_strict returns VOID exactly outside the representable interval.

items.title: BITRAF strict versus modular

formalization.definition: Π maps n to its four residue classes.
formalization.evidence_boundary: Classical modular arithmetic/CRT-style reasoning; project contribution is the chosen multibase tuple.

steps: 420 is divisible by all four moduli, giving periodicity.
If Π(a)=Π(b), then a-b is divisible by 7,10,12,20.
Therefore a-b is divisible by their lcm 420.
Hence the induced map from Z/420Z is injective.

formalization.test: Exhaustively verify 420 distinct tuples for n=0..419 and periodicity n→n+420.
formalization.theorem: Π(n+420)=Π(n) for all n, and Π restricted to Z/420Z is injective.
